user_story: As an AI agent, I want running yunomi with no file to print the agent skill document so I can learn the workflow before serving work.
expected_behavior: When invoked without file arguments in an interactive TTY, yunomi prints the skill document, includes installation guidance, and does not start a review server.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want --skill to print only the skill document so output can be copied into skill files safely.
expected_behavior: yunomi --skill exits 0, starts with the yunomi skill title, includes required workflow sections, and contains no live-log noise.

user_story: As a user, I want empty stdin to fail loudly so broken pipelines are not silently reviewed as empty diffs.
expected_behavior: Empty piped stdin exits 1 and prints usage instead of starting a server.

user_story: As a user, I want --version to report the installed yunomi version so I can verify local/runtime versions.
expected_behavior: yunomi --version exits 0 and prints package version with MoonBit marker.

user_story: As a user, I want --help to explain supported formats and options so I can launch the right review mode.
expected_behavior: yunomi --help exits 0 and lists --port, --host, --no-open, --encoding, --skill, --help, --version, supported formats, stdin diff usage.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want multiple files to open on consecutive ports so I can review a batch in one command.
expected_behavior: Each input file starts a server, using the base port plus index while skipping locked or occupied ports.

user_story: As a user, I want stale or active port locks handled safely so repeated reviews do not collide.
expected_behavior: Server writes a lock for its port, skips active locked ports, removes lock on exit, and does not leave stale lock files after normal exit.

user_story: As a user, I want --host to choose the bind address so local or remote review contexts can be supported.
expected_behavior: --host changes server listen host; 0.0.0.0 is displayed as 127.0.0.1 for local opening while binding all interfaces.

user_story: As a reviewer of Japanese or legacy files, I want encoding detection and --encoding override so source text renders correctly.
expected_behavior: Files decode as UTF-8 when valid, otherwise heuristic Shift-JIS/EUC-JP is used; --encoding/-e overrides detection.

user_story: As an integration test, I want /healthz to report ok so readiness can be verified.
expected_behavior: GET /healthz returns 200 JSON with ok true; HEAD /healthz returns 200 with empty body.

user_story: As a Markdown reviewer, I want relative image/video assets to load while path traversal is blocked.
expected_behavior: Static assets under the reviewed file directory are served with correct MIME types; missing files return 404; traversal outside base returns 403.

user_story: As a browser video player, I want range requests so videos scrub and stream correctly.
expected_behavior: Video range requests return 206 with correct Content-Range and byte length; full video GET returns 200.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want video timeline extraction to reject unsafe paths so arbitrary local files cannot be read.
expected_behavior: /video-timeline rejects path traversal and absolute paths outside the reviewed file base directory.

user_story: As an orchestrating agent, I want comment edits written to a live JSONL log so I can observe review progress in real time.
expected_behavior: POST /comment appends a JSONL event with timestamp/file/type/key/row/col/text/image state, notifies SSE clients, and delete events are accepted.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want common Markdown syntax rendered so reports are readable.
expected_behavior: Headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, code blocks, inline code, ordered/unordered lists, links, images, blockquotes, horizontal rules, tables, and frontmatter parse into expected HTML structures.
evidence: moon test via npm test passed

user_story: As a reviewer, I want unsafe links and scripts escaped or blocked so reports cannot execute arbitrary script.
expected_behavior: javascript: links and unsafe URL/text content do not create executable script tags in the preview.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want Markdown preview beside source lines so I can read rendered content and anchor comments to source lines.
expected_behavior: Markdown mode renders preview pane, source table pane, source rows with data-row attributes, and a recovery modal.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want preview/source scroll positions to stay aligned so I can move between rendered and source context without losing place.
expected_behavior: Preview scrolling syncs the source pane with bounded deltas; selection and card positioning temporarily disable sync to avoid fighting user interactions.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want clicking rendered Markdown elements to select the correct source rows so comments attach to the right text.
expected_behavior: Paragraphs, images, videos, mermaid diagrams, tables, code blocks, list items, blockquotes, headings, and horizontal rules map to source selections or source ranges.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want a preview-only mode so wide reports can be read without the source pane taking space.
expected_behavior: The view toggle changes preview-only class, persists to localStorage, and can be toggled back.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want heading arrows to collapse and expand sections so long reports are easier to scan.
expected_behavior: Heading arrows toggle collapsed state for the section below the heading without breaking comments or preview/source mapping.

user_story: As a report author, I want simple aligned HTML blocks to survive parsing so existing report fragments render acceptably.
expected_behavior: Supported HTML such as p align center is preserved or rendered safely, and subsequent Markdown still parses correctly.
evidence: moon test via npm test passed

user_story: As a report author, I want unresolved questions in frontmatter to render in the submit flow so reviewers answer required prompts.
expected_behavior: Frontmatter yunomi.questions parses id, question, options, resolved state, and answers; submit serializes answers as JSON when present and omits empty answers.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want yunomi to reject media written as plain links so evidence is visible to the human reviewer.
expected_behavior: Markdown files with media paths in [text](path) links exit 1 with actionable fix suggestions; embedded ![alt](path) media is accepted; code spans/fences and non-media links are ignored.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want all images, videos, and diagrams listed in a sidebar so I can jump through evidence quickly.
expected_behavior: Sidebar renders a thumbnail for every detected media item, with visible media content and no separate 45vw viewer panel.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want ArrowUp/ArrowDown and j/k to move through media so I can inspect evidence from the keyboard.
expected_behavior: ArrowDown/j move to next media; ArrowUp/k move to previous media; selection highlights target media; Escape clears active selection and highlight.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want ArrowLeft/ArrowRight or h/l to move within an inline video timeline without changing which media item is selected.
expected_behavior: When a video timeline is focused or selected via sidebar, horizontal keys seek between timeline thumbnails while keeping the same active media item.

user_story: As a reviewer entering text or submitting, I want media/comment shortcuts disabled so typing does not move the UI unexpectedly.
expected_behavior: When submit modal, recovery modal, question modal, comment card, inputs, or textareas are active, hjkl/arrow media navigation and i/Enter comment shortcuts do not trigger background navigation.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want inline videos to show scene thumbnails so I can jump to meaningful moments without opening fullscreen.
expected_behavior: Inline video timeline reserves layout space, loads thumbnails when visible, shows time labels below thumbnails, and labels do not overlap thumbnail images.
evidence: video_timeline.ts 15 passed; added to npm test route

user_story: As a reviewer, I want clicking preview images to open a fullscreen view so I can inspect images closely.
expected_behavior: Clicking an image opens fullscreen overlay; Escape or backdrop click closes it; source line remains/comment target can be selected.
observed_errors: pr_verification initially expected stale #modal-submit selector after submit modal opened

user_story: As a reviewer, I want clicking videos to open fullscreen playback with timeline thumbnails and keyboard controls so video evidence is inspectable.
expected_behavior: Clicking video opens fullscreen viewer; timeline labels arrive; fullscreen keyboard controls work; settings panel opens and selected state updates.
current_automated_coverage: v2/e2e/media_sidebar_regression.ts partially; v2/e2e/video_timeline.ts not in npm test
evidence: npm test covers viewer open/settings; video_timeline.ts has separate deeper coverage

user_story: As a report author, I want Mermaid diagrams to render inline so architecture and flow diagrams are readable.
expected_behavior: Mermaid code fences render as diagrams, appear in the media sidebar, and can be inspected without breaking normal Markdown source mapping.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want large Mermaid diagrams to open fullscreen with pan/zoom minimap so complex diagrams remain readable.
expected_behavior: Fullscreen Mermaid minimap follows visible region after open, pan, and zoom within tolerance.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want clicking a cell/line/preview target to open a comment card so I can add, update, or delete feedback anchored to content.
expected_behavior: Comment card opens near the target, shows target preview, allows text entry, save, delete, and selected-line copy where applicable.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want a consistent comment button on markdown, image, video, and timeline targets so I do not need to discover click-only comment behavior.
expected_behavior: Comment buttons are installed on eligible preview targets, hidden from extracted target text, stay behind dialogs, and open comment cards for markdown, image, video, and timeline thumbnail targets.

user_story: As a keyboard user, I want i or Enter to open the selected comment target so I can comment without using the mouse.
expected_behavior: i and Enter open the card for the current selected target; shortcuts are blocked while dialogs or text inputs are active.

user_story: As a table reviewer, I want Shift+h/l to move horizontally between cells so I can comment on adjacent table values efficiently.
expected_behavior: Starting from a selected table cell, Shift+l moves right and Shift+h moves left; Enter opens the selected cell's comment card.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want removed unstable Shift+j/k behavior to stay removed so vertical oscillation does not return.
expected_behavior: Shift+j/k do not move comment selection and do not double-fire media sidebar movement; normal j/k media navigation remains active.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want to drag across rows/cells to create batch comments so multi-line or rectangular feedback is efficient.
expected_behavior: Dragging selects rectangular table regions or multiple rows, then opens or anchors a batch comment to the selected range.
evidence: feature_matrix_regression.ts passed for multi-row drag selection

user_story: As a reviewer, I want in-progress comments to be auto-saved so accidental reloads or closes do not lose work.
expected_behavior: Comments are saved to localStorage with timestamp, old/incompatible data is rejected, restore/discard modal appears, restore skips empty entries, and expired data is handled.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want to paste an image into a comment so visual feedback can accompany text.
expected_behavior: Comment card has an image preview area; paste renders data:image preview; saved comments show an image indicator.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want Cmd/Ctrl+Enter or Submit & Exit to open a final review dialog so I can choose a verdict and summary.
expected_behavior: Keyboard shortcut and button open submit modal; comment input Cmd/Ctrl+Enter saves comment without opening submit modal.

user_story: As an AI agent, I want submit output as structured YAML so I can parse decision, summary, answers, and comments.
expected_behavior: Submit prints action, file, mode, comments, summary, decision, and optional answers without [object Object] coercion; comments quote source value.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want approve, request changes, handoff, and final approve actions represented in output so agents can continue the right workflow.
expected_behavior: Submitting each decision/action exits server and includes the expected action/decision marker in YAML.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want to attach images in the final submit dialog so final verdict can include visual proof or context.
expected_behavior: Submit modal supports pasted images with visible counter and maximum attachment limit.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want history to persist by file so I can revisit recent review submissions.
expected_behavior: Submissions save to ~/.yunomi/history keyed by file path hash, trim to 50 entries, /history returns JSON, and UI history panel opens/closes.

user_story: As a user, I want reloads not to terminate review, but final close to flush draft and exit when appropriate.
expected_behavior: Browser reload keeps server alive; closing the latest active page exits and flushes draft; stale prior instances are ignored.

user_story: As a user, I want old tabs from a prior server session to retire when a new server reuses the port so stale tabs do not submit to the wrong session.
expected_behavior: SSE hello provides instance id; same server reconnect keeps id; reused port gets new id; stale tabs close or park on about:blank and do not show new session content.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want CSV files rendered as a table so I can comment on rows and cells.
expected_behavior: CSV files parse RFC4180-style content, render table rows/cells with data-row attributes, include recovery modal, and display cell values.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want TSV files rendered like CSV tables so tab-separated data can be reviewed.
expected_behavior: TSV files use tab delimiter, render table cells, and support the same commenting/recovery behavior as CSV.
observed_errors: TSV rendered as table but exposed __YUNOMI_MODE__ as csv before this pass

user_story: As a reviewer, I want plain text files rendered line-by-line so arbitrary notes/logs can be reviewed.
expected_behavior: Plain text fallback splits content into rows and renders a table-like line review surface with comments available per line.

user_story: As a code reviewer, I want unified diff files or stdin diffs rendered with file/hunk structure so changes are readable.
expected_behavior: Unified diff parser handles git prefixes, multiple files, hunk headers, and builds syntax-highlighted diff HTML.
evidence: moon test via npm test passed

user_story: As a user, I want .diff/.patch files and stdin diff to open in diff mode so git changes can be reviewed.
expected_behavior: Diff files and piped stdin generate diff-mode HTML and support submit output; smoke checks stdin and diff server behavior.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want large files collapsed and binary files sorted last so huge diffs stay navigable.
expected_behavior: Diff view collapses files over 500 lines and moves binary files to the end of the file list.
observed_errors: Large diff collapse and binary sort were README-level expectations without direct E2E before this pass

user_story: As a reviewer, I want light/dark theme toggle persisted so review remains comfortable across reloads.
expected_behavior: Theme button toggles data-theme, persists to localStorage, and toggles back correctly.

user_story: As a maintainer, I want npm packaging to include only runtime dist files and metadata so users install a small working CLI.
expected_behavior: prepack builds release JS, writes executable dist/server/server.js, copies dist/ui/ui.js, and npm pack includes LICENSE, README files, dist files, package.json.

user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want the plugin bundle to include skills, agents, hooks, and docs so yunomi workflows can be installed.
expected_behavior: plugin/ contains README, skills, agents, hooks, hook handlers, and skill docs matching README plugin structure.
evidence: feature_matrix_regression.ts static plugin asset validation passed

user_story: As an AI agent, I want bundled do/done/tiny-do/tiny-done skills so task start, evidence, review, and completion workflows are repeatable.
expected_behavior: Skills exist under plugin/skills and describe task start/completion workflows with verification and yunomi review expectations.
evidence: feature_matrix_regression.ts static task skill validation passed

user_story: As an agent running long review servers, I want exit-notifier to report command completion back to the active pane so users know when jobs exit.
expected_behavior: watch-exit-notify.sh wraps commands, captures exit status/output, and can target Herdr/tmux panes safely.

user_story: As an agent, I want bundled webapp-testing guidance so frontend changes are verified with Playwright before reporting completion.
expected_behavior: webapp-testing skill exists and instructs using permanent e2e files or Playwright verification for local apps.
evidence: feature_matrix_regression.ts static webapp-testing skill validation passed

user_story: As a reviewer, I want Mermaid diagrams to expose the same top-right comment button as Markdown text, images, videos, and video thumbnails so every preview artifact has one obvious comment path.
expected_behavior: Rendered Mermaid containers receive a single top-right comment button, the obsolete Mermaid fullscreen button is absent because diagram click opens fullscreen, the comment button opens the comment card for the diagram source range, and keyboard target enumeration includes Mermaid containers.
evidence: comment_shortcuts_regression.ts verifies Mermaid button presence, fullscreen button absence, and click-to-comment behavior; media_sidebar_regression.ts verifies diagram click still opens fullscreen

user_story: As a reviewer reading submitted YAML, I want each comment value to identify the exact reviewed target so the feedback is actionable without reopening the browser state.
expected_behavior: Submitted comments include a client-provided value: table-cell comments include Markdown table row/column and cell text, video-thumbnail comments include timestamp and video src, and both include the source Markdown row.
evidence: comment_shortcuts_regression.ts submits table-cell and video-thumbnail comments and asserts the verdict YAML contains reconstructable values
